claims.text: The as-deposited non-equiatomic FeMnNiGeSi alloy is in an ordered single-phase hexagonal state.
The alloy undergoes a sharp first-order magnetostructural transition.
The first-order transition produces a large magnetic entropy change.
The as-deposited material has a low surface-to-volume ratio that limits heat exchange.
Interface kinetics between transforming and untransformed regions govern the magnetocaloric response during low-field cooling cycles.
Interface kinetics between transforming and untransformed regions govern hysteresis during low-field cooling cycles.
Changing deposition rate or applying a mild post-deposition thermal treatment will modify grain size and defect density.
Grain boundaries and other interfacial defects mediate nucleation of the phase transformation.
Grain boundaries and other interfacial defects mediate propagation of the phase transformation.
Altering deposition parameters can reduce interfacial nucleation-energy barriers during the magnetostructural transition.
Reduced interfacial barriers will promote smoother phase evolution during magnetic-field cycling.
Smoother phase evolution will decrease hysteretic losses.
Optimized deposition conditions will broaden the magnetostructural transition relative to the as-deposited baseline.
Optimized deposition conditions will produce narrower hysteresis loops relative to the as-deposited baseline.
The reduction in hysteresis can occur while maintaining a high magnetocaloric entropy change.
The proposed deposition optimization will enhance effective heat exchange.
The predicted improvements are restricted to low applied fields near the transition and to moderate processing changes that do not induce secondary phases or substantially alter composition.
